subject: computer_networks
title: Computer Networks Lab
note: Sample questions written for VivaBridge. No real exam data.

concepts.syn: Client sends a SYN segment with its initial sequence number to request a connection
concepts.syn_ack: Server replies SYN-ACK: acknowledges the client's sequence number and sends its own
concepts.final_ack: Client sends a final ACK so the server knows its SYN was received; only then is the connection established
concepts.sequence_numbers: Each side picks an initial sequence number so bytes can be ordered and acknowledged
concepts.nonce: A number used once, so old messages cannot be replayed
concepts.replay_attack: An attacker re-sends a captured valid message to trick the receiver
concepts.subnet_mask: Bits that separate the network part of an IP address from the host part
concepts.network_address: The address that identifies the subnet itself, found by ANDing the IP with the mask

questions.rubric_notes: Names the three steps in order (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), who sends each, and that the connection is established only after the final ACK.

questions.text: Why does TCP need three messages to open a connection instead of two?
questions.rubric_notes: Both sides must confirm the other's initial sequence number. With two messages the server never learns whether its SYN reached the client. It also prevents stale duplicate connection requests.

questions.text: What is the role of sequence numbers during TCP connection establishment?
questions.rubric_notes: Each side chooses an initial sequence number and sends it in its SYN; the other side acknowledges ISN+1. This enables ordering and reliable delivery.

questions.text: A client sends SYN and receives SYN-ACK, but its final ACK is lost. What happens?
questions.rubric_notes: The server stays in SYN-RECEIVED (half-open) and retransmits SYN-ACK after a timeout. The connection is not established on the server side until an ACK arrives.

questions.text: What is a nonce and why is it used in network security protocols?
questions.rubric_notes: A number used only once (random or a counter). It makes each message fresh so a captured message cannot be replayed.

questions.text: How can an attacker perform a replay attack, and how does a protocol defend against it?
questions.rubric_notes: The attacker records a valid message and re-sends it later. Defences include nonces, timestamps or sequence numbers so the receiver rejects repeats.

questions.text: What is a subnet mask, and how do you find the network address of 192.168.10.37/24?
questions.rubric_notes: The mask 255.255.255.0 separates network and host bits. AND the IP with the mask to get 192.168.10.0.

questions.text: Why do two hosts need to know whether they are on the same subnet?
questions.rubric_notes: A host compares network addresses (IP AND mask). On the same network it delivers directly; otherwise it sends to the default gateway (router).
